{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjccM8AAAABiBlANg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IfzhLZTkk", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3If", "number": 142, "title": "Match the virtual controller to WonderSwan hardware and add per-cartridge orientation controls", "body": "## Problem

The current touch controller exposes the correct eleven game-input buttons, but its arrangement is not faithful to the physical WonderSwan. In particular, the two directional groups are placed side by side in a narrow portrait viewport and on opposite sides of the screen in the compact landscape viewport. The physical console instead places Y above X on the left in its normal horizontal position. The directional groups also do not rotate with the vertical cartridge presentation.

The physical orientation of a phone and the intended orientation of a WonderSwan game are different concepts. A user commonly holds a phone upright while playing a horizontal WonderSwan game. Rotating the phone must not change the intended orientation or rotate the logical controls.

Redesign the virtual controller around the original hardware's spatial relationships and make horizontal/vertical game presentation independently selectable, defaulting to the cartridge header.

## Expected outcome

- Retain exactly eleven game-input buttons: X1–X4, Y1–Y4, A, B and Start, with hardware-faithful spatial relationships and clearly readable labels.
- Default to the ROM's orientation metadata. Offer a small **Orientation** setting with **Auto (ROM header)**, **Horizontal**, and **Vertical**. A manual override changes both the screen and virtual controller together, without restarting the game.
- Remember an explicit orientation preference per raw ROM identity in browser-local storage; Auto is the default for each new cartridge. Changing the phone's physical orientation affects responsive sizing and placement only, never the chosen game orientation or logical input mapping.
- Prioritize comfortable gameplay while holding a phone upright, for both horizontal and vertical cartridges. Support landscape phone viewports and fullscreen as well. Preserve the existing streamlined player layout and controls.
- Keep existing keyboard mappings, eleven input masks, independent simultaneous input, and cartridge/save behavior unchanged. No added game buttons, duplicated Sound/Power controls, elaborate console shell, or new framework.

## Context and reproduction

Baseline: `main` at [bb6f672](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/commit/bb6f672a1ec40dd688d01a1f6b312b28ad8e7359), after layout PR #137. Check current main before implementation.

- [`web/index.html`](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/web/index.html): `#touch-controls` contains two `.dpad` groups and `.action-row`. Physical button identities are expressed by `data-button`.
- [`web/src/style.css`](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/web/src/style.css): `.dpad` currently places buttons in an unrotated four-way grid; base touch layout wraps the groups, while compact landscape places X on the left and Y/actions on the right. The canvas currently rotates counterclockwise for vertical presentation.
- [`web/src/main.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/web/src/main.ts): `refresh()`, `sizeScreen()`, `focusGame()`, `machine.orientation()`, keyboard `bindings`, `updateButtons()`, `clearKeys()`, pointer capture and pointer cancellation. Use one effective presentation orientation consistently instead of treating viewport orientation as the game orientation.
- [`crates/ws-web/src/lib.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/crates/ws-web/src/lib.rs): `orientation()` exposes cartridge header metadata. Keep this API's meaning and the native 224×144 framebuffer unchanged.
- [`web/src/saves.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/web/src/saves.ts): existing raw-ROM SHA-256 identity. Use that identity for a separate namespaced orientation preference, not the filename or a console-global setting.
- Use existing independent CC0 horizontal/vertical keypad fixtures in `fixtures/generated/` and existing browser input/layout checks. Verify physical layout and input convention against public hardware documentation, e.g. [WSdev Wiki](https://ws.nesdev.org/wiki/Main_Page) and photographs/manual illustrations of WonderSwan, WonderSwan Color and SwanCrystal. These are references for control geometry and numbering, not assets to copy or distribute.
- Related #136 / #137 (recent streamlined responsive layout), #138 / #139 (remembered ROM picker), #140 / #141 (original IPL). The latter two changes are in progress at the time of writing. Integrate with whichever versions land on main, including remembered-ROM selection, without implementing their unrelated functionality or introducing duplicate load paths.

To reproduce the current layout: load a horizontal and a vertical keypad fixture in a narrow touch viewport and a short landscape touch viewport; observe that the relative X/Y arrangement is based on responsive CSS and that individual button positions do not rotate with the cartridge.

### Hardware layout and button identities

All three physical models share the same eleven game-input identities. Sound and Power are console controls, not additional game keypad inputs; the existing player toolbar already handles sound and restart.

Use the following agreed reference arrangement in the normal horizontal game orientation:

```text
   Y1       +-------------------+
Y4    Y2    |                   |
   Y3       |    224 × 144      |
            |                   |
   X1       +-------------------+     A
X4    X2                         B
   X3              START
```

- Both directional groups belong to the left-hand side, with **Y above X**. Each group contains four distinct controls: 1 at top, 2 at right, 3 at bottom, 4 at left.
- A is upper-right relative to B; B is lower-left relative to A. Start is a distinct secondary control, generally below the screen.
- When playing a horizontal game on an upright phone, place the screen above a compact control area, maintaining Y above X on the left and A/B on the right, with Start clearly reachable. On a wide phone, place both directional groups beside the left of the display when room permits, and actions on the right. Do not revert to X and Y on opposite sides simply because the viewport is wide.

The vertical game orientation corresponds to rotating the physical console counterclockwise 90 degrees, consistent with the existing canvas presentation. Y is now the lower-left group and X the lower-right group. The button identities rotate with their groups; do not change the hardware bits:

| Visual direction | Horizontal | Vertical (90° CCW) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Up | X1 / Y1 | X2 / Y2 |
| Right | X2 / Y2 | X3 / Y3 |
| Down | X3 / Y3 | X4 / Y4 |
| Left | X4 / Y4 | X1 / Y1 |

```text
              A   B
       +-------------+
       |             |  START
       |  144 × 224  |
       |             |
       +-------------+
   Y2                    X2
Y1    Y3              X1    X3
   Y4                    X4
```

The diagram establishes physical relationships, not mandatory pixel coordinates. A/B and Start move to the right/upper area relative to the vertical screen in accordance with the rotated console; keep them reachable without obscuring the game. Adapt the exact spacing to phone width, height and safe areas while preserving the directional groups' order, rotated internal identities and A/B relationship (A above-left of B in the rotated layout). Do not require a literal replica of the console shell. On constrained viewports, favor readable usable controls and an honest scrollable layout over clipped targets or an unreadably small game screen.

### Orientation preference and UI

1. Introduce a presentation-only setting in Help or a similarly unobtrusive existing settings area, labeled **Orientation**. The three options are:
   - **Auto (ROM header)** — use the actual header-reported horizontal/vertical orientation; default.
   - **Horizontal** — native 224×144 presentation and horizontal hardware controller arrangement.
   - **Vertical** — counterclockwise 90-degree presentation at 144×224 and corresponding rotated hardware controller arrangement.
2. Derive one effective game orientation from the selected preference and current cartridge metadata. Apply it to screen bounds/aspect ratio, canvas rotation, touch controller layout, directional labels, sizing, display effects and fullscreen presentation. Never derive it from `screen.orientation`, viewport aspect ratio or a device motion/orientation sensor. CSS media queries may adapt the responsive layout, not determine logical orientation or button assignment.
3. Store explicit preferences using a separate versioned WonderSwan-specific localStorage namespace keyed by the existing **raw ROM SHA-256**. Identical bytes under different filenames share the setting; different bytes with the same name do not. Restore on every successful load (including #138 saved cartridges), revisit, restart and compatible console change. Switching to Auto removes/clears the explicit override. Invalid or unavailable storage falls back gracefully to Auto without blocking play. Never modify cartridge SRAM/EEPROM, RTC, console data, ROM library records or existing audio/display keys. The no-cartridge state defaults to Auto/horizontal and must not write a bogus per-cartridge record.
4. Selecting an orientation must not reload, restart, reset or change the emulated console model, cartridge header, native frame dimensions, core timing, save identity, or existing Play/Pause intent. Clear held inputs before moving buttons so a stale captured pointer cannot become a different pressed direction. Preserve existing Help-modal pause/resume and focus behavior. Changing the setting while paused or playing should update the presentation immediately (including the paused frame) and reset presentation-only history only where required.
5. Keep the main toolbar and cartridge area uncluttered. Update Help and README to explain game orientation vs phone orientation and the relationship between physical X/Y labels and visual directions. Do not introduce a device-orientation permission, forced browser orientation lock, extra permanent settings panel, or per-model orientation setting.

### Touch interaction and responsive design

- Keep eleven semantic buttons with the existing masks: X1=16, X2=32, X3=64, X4=128; Y1=256, Y2=512, Y3=1024, Y4=2048; A=4, B=8, Start=2. Preserve physical IDs, rather than remapping bits according to screen position. The unchanged keyboard bindings remain tied to those physical identities.
- Make each direction visually distinct, using a restrained rounded/triangular or directional shape inspired by the hardware. If arrows are shown, they must match the visual direction in the effective orientation, not a stale unrotated arrow. Accessible names identify the physical button and its actual keyboard binding; explain rotation in Help.
- Preserve multi-touch union semantics across both keypads and action buttons, independent pointer release, keyboard+touch input, pointercancel/lostpointercapture and clearing on pause, Help, visibility change, cartridge replacement, model change and orientation/layout changes where needed. Do not add a second duplicate set of input elements for another orientation. Keep active visual feedback and keyboard accessibility.
- Maintain at least 44×44 CSS pixel touch targets and reasonable separation whenever feasible; do not achieve the design by shrinking actual hit targets. Prevent overlapping buttons, scroll gestures while pressing game controls, accidental page interactions, clipped controls, and screen-overlay hit regions. Use responsive layout, safe-area padding and existing fullscreen infrastructure; allow normal page scrolling outside controls when content truly does not fit.
- In normal mobile portrait mode, prioritize the game screen and complete touch controller. Do not place a large cartridge panel or unrelated controls between essential gameplay controls if doing so pushes them unnecessarily below the fold. Maintain access to the current cartridge, picker, Console selector, toolbar, error/status notices and audio recovery.
- Preserve the light theme, desktop keyboard play, coarse-pointer behavior, empty/paused states, all four display modes (including existing Retro CRT default and LCD portrait handling), native screen proportions, fullscreen access/exit, and existing player error recovery. Avoid unrelated shader, core, firmware or ROM-library changes.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Eleven unique touch controls retain the existing hardware input masks. Geometry tests check Y above X on the left for horizontal presentation, X/Y group internal order, diagonal A/B relationship, and the rotated vertical arrangement (Y left, X right; 2/3/4/1 clockwise from top). No extra game-input button or duplicate hidden active controller.
- [ ] Using real Wasm and the existing horizontal/vertical CC0 keypad fixtures, Auto follows each cartridge header, Horizontal/Vertical override it, and screen plus controls update together. Verify the actual 224:144 or 144:224 displayed aspect ratio and correct counterclockwise rotation, not just CSS class names. Both horizontal and vertical overrides work on an opposite-orientation ROM.
- [ ] Test the same horizontal game while a phone is held portrait and landscape, and the same vertical game in both viewports; resizing/rotating the viewport never changes the effective orientation or logical button assignments. Manual override remains effective across resize/fullscreen.
- [ ] Verify per-ROM override retention on reload/revisit, same-content/different filename, different-content/same filename, restart and compatible model change. Auto clears the override. Simulate unavailable or malformed local storage and confirm normal Auto gameplay without disturbing existing progress records. If remembered-ROM picker #138 has landed, include selection from it in applicable coverage; otherwise do not block this issue on its merge.
- [ ] Real guest input probes verify each button's hardware mask in both presentations, including multiple simultaneous directions/action buttons and combined keyboard/touch use. Test independent release, pointer cancellation and switching orientation while a control is held; no stuck/reassigned input, reset or unexpected resume. Preserve existing pause, Help, fullscreen and visibility behavior.
- [ ] Test mobile viewport layouts at representative 375×812 and 812×375, plus a short/narrow 320×568 or equivalent constrained viewport. Check control and screen bounds, no overlapping/clipped targets, 44px hit targets, accessible names, viewport/safe-area behavior, sensible scrolling and reachable controls, status/ROM error recovery and audio enable action. Include portrait-phone horizontal gameplay as the primary case. Record a small set of actual screenshots showing both game orientations in phone portrait and landscape; use original fixture ROMs only.
- [ ] Preserve existing display-mode and orientation rendering checks, touch/keyboard tests, browser loading and persistence behavior. Orientation changes are presentation-only and do not require or introduce Rust core changes. Add focused browser regressions to the existing suites rather than duplicate unrelated checks.
- [ ] Update README and Help with the actual orientation choices, per-cartridge behavior, hardware button labels and independence from device rotation.
- [ ] Run applicable production-preview checks in `web`: `npm ci`, `npm run build:wasm` if needed, `npm run build`, `npm run test:browser`, `npm run test:compat`, plus `git diff --check`. Follow the repository's test/CI performance principles; reuse builds, run Rust/fixture checks only if their sources or applicable behavior change, and record actual validation results and limitations. No physical device, proprietary firmware, or commercial ROM is required.

## Optional validation

Test on mobile WebKit or a physical smartphone if available, especially multitouch, short landscape and safe-area behavior. Report actual observations without claiming physical-device testing if none was performed.

## Required post-merge verification

After implementation and mandatory pre-merge acceptance are complete, merge and close the Issue following the repository lifecycle. Verify the GitHub Pages deployment of the merge revision, and record its workflow URL and revision. On the published player, load the original horizontal and vertical keypad fixtures, verify Auto and manual overrides, hold the phone-shaped browser viewport upright for both orientations, resize to landscape without changing the selected orientation, and confirm actual guest button responses. Record what was actually tested and any limitations.
